review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

6:1.sourceText: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀπῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης τῆς Γαλιλαίας τῆς Τιβεριάδος.
6:1.targetText: After this, Jesus crossed to the other side of the Sea of Galilee (that is, the Sea of Tiberias).

groups.note: θαλάσσης is understood again with τῆς Τιβεριάδος, where English repeats "Sea".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English marks the second name as another name for the same sea.

6:2.sourceText: ἠκολούθει δὲ αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς, ὅτι ἑώρων τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει ἐπὶ τῶν ἀσθενούντων.
6:2.targetText: A large crowd followed Him because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick.

groups.note: BSB's Greek has another verb of seeing here, with the same meaning.
Article and participle τῶν ἀσθενούντων "those who were sick" form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed in English.
The relative pronoun ἅ ("which") is left implicit in English.

6:3.sourceText: ἀνῆλθεν δὲ εἰς τὸ ὄρος Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐκεῖ ἐκάθητο μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ.
6:3.targetText: Then Jesus went up on the mountain and sat down with His disciples.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverb ἐκεῖ ("there") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:4.sourceText: ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα, ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
6:4.targetText: Now the Jewish Feast of the Passover was near.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins "Feast" and "the Passover" with "of"; the Greek sets the two nouns side by side.

6:5.sourceText: ἐπάρας οὖν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ θεασάμενος ὅτι πολὺς ὄχλος ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτὸν, λέγει πρὸς Φίλιππον Πόθεν ἀγοράσωμεν ἄρτους ἵνα φάγωσιν οὗτοι;
6:5.targetText: When Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward Him, He said to Philip, “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”

groups.note: ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς ("lifting up his eyes") supplies the When-clause, rendered "looked up".

unmappedSource.reason: The connective οὖν is not separately expressed; When belongs to the participle.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ὅτι ("that") is not rendered; BSB writes "saw a large crowd coming".

6:6.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγεν πειράζων αὐτόν· αὐτὸς γὰρ ᾔδει τί ἔμελλεν ποιεῖν.
6:6.targetText: But He was asking this to test him, for He knew what He was about to do.

6:7.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ ὁ Φίλιππος Διακοσίων δηναρίων ἄρτοι οὐκ ἀρκοῦσιν αὐτοῖς, ἵνα ἕκαστος βραχύ τι λάβῃ.
6:7.targetText: Philip answered, “Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece.”

groups.note: ἀρκοῦσιν ("are enough") is rendered "would … enough".
The dative αὐτοῖς ("for them") is merged into "for each of them".

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the buying implied by the genitive of price Διακοσίων δηναρίων ("bread worth two hundred denarii").

6:8.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ εἷς ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς Σίμωνος Πέτρου
6:8.targetText: One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to Him,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:9.sourceText: Ἔστιν παιδάριον ὧδε ὃς ἔχει πέντε ἄρτους κριθίνους καὶ δύο ὀψάρια· ἀλλὰ ταῦτα τί ἐστιν εἰς τοσούτους;
6:9.targetText: “Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish. But what difference will these make among so many?”

groups.note: The relative clause ὃς ἔχει ("who has") is rendered "with".
The Greek asks "what are these for so many?"; BSB recasts ἐστιν as "will … make".

6:10.sourceText: εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ποιήσατε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἀναπεσεῖν. ἦν δὲ χόρτος πολὺς ἐν τῷ τόπῳ. ἀνέπεσαν οὖν οἱ ἄνδρες τὸν ἀριθμὸν ὡς πεντακισχίλιοι.
6:10.targetText: “Have the people sit down,” Jesus said. Now there was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, about five thousand of them.

groups.note: The accusative τὸν ἀριθμόν ("in number") is rendered "of them" after the count.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:11.sourceText: ἔλαβεν οὖν τοὺς ἄρτους ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εὐχαριστήσας διέδωκεν τοῖς ἀνακειμένοις, ὁμοίως καὶ ἐκ τῶν ὀψαρίων ὅσον ἤθελον.
6:11.targetText: Then Jesus took the loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted.

groups.note: The καί joining "took" and "distributed" stands before the last verb of BSB's series.
Article and participle τοῖς ἀνακειμένοις ("those reclining") form one unit.
ὁμοίως καί ("likewise also") is rendered "and", as BSB joins the fish to the loaves.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The partitive ἐκ ("some of") is not rendered; BSB makes the fish an object of "took".

6:12.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐνεπλήσθησαν, λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Συναγάγετε τὰ περισσεύσαντα κλάσματα, ἵνα μή τι ἀπόληται.
6:12.targetText: And when everyone was full, He said to His disciples, “Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted.”

groups.note: The dative τοῖς μαθηταῖς supplies "to".
μή τι ("not anything") is rendered "nothing".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:13.sourceText: συνήγαγον οὖν, καὶ ἐγέμισαν δώδεκα κοφίνους κλασμάτων ἐκ τῶν πέντε ἄρτων τῶν κριθίνων ἃ ἐπερίσσευσαν τοῖς βεβρωκόσιν.
6:13.targetText: So they collected them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten.

groups.note: The relative clause ἃ ἐπερίσσευσαν ("which were left over") is rendered "left over".
Article and participle τοῖς βεβρωκόσιν form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of "collected".
English makes "pieces" definite; κλασμάτων has no article.

6:14.sourceText: Οἱ οὖν ἄνθρωποι ἰδόντες ὃ ἐποίησεν σημεῖον ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ προφήτης ὁ ἐρχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον.
6:14.targetText: When the people saw the sign that Jesus had performed, they began to say, “Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world.”

groups.note: The participle ἰδόντες supplies the When-clause.
Article and participle ὁ ἐρχόμενος ("the one coming") form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective οὖν is not separately expressed; When belongs to the participle.
Recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name; the Greek has only the verb ending.

6:15.sourceText: Ἰησοῦς οὖν γνοὺς ὅτι μέλλουσιν ἔρχεσθαι καὶ ἁρπάζειν αὐτὸν ἵνα ποιήσωσιν βασιλέα, ἀνεχώρησεν πάλιν εἰς τὸ ὄρος αὐτὸς μόνος.
6:15.targetText: Then Jesus, realizing that they were about to come and make Him king by force, withdrew again to a mountain by Himself.

groups.note: ἁρπάζειν ("to seize") is expressed as "by force"; BSB merges "seize Him to make Him king".
αὐτὸς μόνος ("He alone") is rendered "by Himself".

unmappedSource.reason: ἵνα ("in order to") is not rendered; BSB merges the purpose clause into "make Him king by force".
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:16.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ ὀψία ἐγένετο, κατέβησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν,
6:16.targetText: When evening came, His disciples went down to the sea,

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:17.sourceText: καὶ ἐμβάντες εἰς πλοῖον ἤρχοντο πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς Καφαρναούμ. καὶ σκοτία ἤδη ἐγεγόνει καὶ οὔπω ἐληλύθει πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς,
6:17.targetText: got into a boat, and started across the sea to Capernaum. It was already dark, and Jesus had not yet gone out to them.

groups.note: The καί joining "went down" (verse 16) and "started" stands before the last verb of BSB's series.
ἐμβάντες εἰς ("embarking into") is rendered "got into".
The imperfect ἤρχοντο ("were going") is rendered "started across".

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed; BSB begins a new sentence.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:18.sourceText: ἥ τε θάλασσα ἀνέμου μεγάλου πνέοντος διεγείρετο.
6:18.targetText: A strong wind was blowing, and the sea grew agitated.

6:19.sourceText: ἐληλακότες οὖν ὡς σταδίους εἴκοσι πέντε ἢ τριάκοντα θεωροῦσιν τὸν Ἰησοῦν περιπατοῦντα ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐγγὺς τοῦ πλοίου γινόμενον, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.
6:19.targetText: When they had rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus approaching the boat, walking on the sea—and they were terrified.

groups.note: The participle ἐληλακότες supplies the When-clause.
σταδίους εἴκοσι πέντε ἢ τριάκοντα ("twenty-five or thirty stadia") is converted to miles.
ἐγγὺς … γινόμενον ("coming near") is rendered "approaching".

unmappedSource.reason: The connective οὖν is not separately expressed; When belongs to the participle.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
Connective not rendered; BSB puts "approaching the boat" before "walking on the sea".

6:20.sourceText: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἐγώ εἰμι, μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
6:20.targetText: But Jesus spoke up: “It is I; do not be afraid.”

groups.note: In ὁ δέ ("but he") the article is a pronoun; BSB names Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτοῖς ("to them") is not rendered.

6:21.sourceText: ἤθελον οὖν λαβεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ εὐθέως ἐγένετο τὸ πλοῖον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς εἰς ἣν ὑπῆγον.
6:21.targetText: Then they were willing to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading.

groups.note: ἐγένετο … ἐπί ("came to be at") is rendered "reached".
εἰς ἥν ("to which") is rendered "where".

6:22.sourceText: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ὁ ὄχλος ὁ ἑστηκὼς πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἶδον ὅτι πλοιάριον ἄλλο οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖ εἰ μὴ ἕν, καὶ ὅτι οὐ συνεισῆλθεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἀλλὰ μόνοι οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθον·
6:22.targetText: The next day, the crowd that had remained on the other side of the sea realized that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus had not boarded it with His disciples, but they had gone away alone.

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ ἑστηκώς ("the one standing") form one unit.
πλοιάριον ἄλλο οὐκ … εἰ μὴ ἕν ("no other boat … except one") is rendered "only one boat".
συνεισῆλθεν … εἰς ("went in with … into") is rendered "boarded … with".
τὸ πλοῖον ("the boat") is rendered "it".
οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ("His disciples") is rendered "they".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:23.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἦλθεν πλοιάρια ἐκ Τιβεριάδος ἐγγὺς τοῦ τόπου ὅπου ἔφαγον τὸν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσαντος τοῦ Κυρίου.
6:23.targetText: However, some boats from Tiberias landed near the place where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.

groups.note: The genitive absolute εὐχαριστήσαντος τοῦ Κυρίου supplies the after-clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

6:24.sourceText: ὅτε οὖν εἶδεν ὁ ὄχλος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκεῖ οὐδὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, ἐνέβησαν αὐτοὶ εἰς τὰ πλοιάρια καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ ζητοῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
6:24.targetText: So when the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor His disciples were there, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him.

groups.note: τὸν Ἰησοῦν ("Jesus") is rendered "Him".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:25.sourceText: καὶ εὑρόντες αὐτὸν πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἶπον αὐτῷ Ῥαββεί, πότε ὧδε γέγονας;
6:25.targetText: When they found Him on the other side of the sea, they asked Him, “Rabbi, when did You get here?”

groups.note: The participle εὑρόντες supplies the When-clause.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.

6:26.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ζητεῖτέ με οὐχ ὅτι εἴδετε σημεῖα, ἀλλ’ ὅτι ἐφάγετε ἐκ τῶν ἄρτων καὶ ἐχορτάσθητε.
6:26.targetText: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not because you saw these signs that you are looking for Me, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη … καὶ εἶπεν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb replied.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτοῖς ("to them") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The partitive ἐκ ("some of") is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English cleft frame ("it is not because … that …") with no Greek counterpart.
English cleft frame ("it is not because … that …") with no Greek counterpart.
English adds "these"; the Greek has only σημεῖα ("signs").

6:27.sourceText: ἐργάζεσθε μὴ τὴν βρῶσιν τὴν ἀπολλυμένην, ἀλλὰ τὴν βρῶσιν τὴν μένουσαν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἣν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑμῖν δώσει· τοῦτον γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐσφράγισεν ὁ Θεός.
6:27.targetText: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.”

groups.note: ἐργάζεσθε ("work for") is understood again with the second object.
The article with the participle ἀπολλυμένην is rendered "that perishes".

targetPhrases.text: has placed His seal of approval

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:28.sourceText: εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτόν Τί ποιῶμεν ἵνα ἐργαζώμεθα τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Θεοῦ;
6:28.targetText: Then they inquired, “What must we do to perform the works of God?”

unmappedSource.reason: πρὸς αὐτόν ("to Him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:29.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ ἔργον τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἵνα πιστεύητε εἰς ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ἐκεῖνος.
6:29.targetText: Jesus replied, “The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent.”

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη … καὶ εἶπεν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb replied.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτοῖς ("to them") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:30.sourceText: εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ Τί οὖν ποιεῖς σὺ σημεῖον, ἵνα ἴδωμεν καὶ πιστεύσωμέν σοι; τί ἐργάζῃ;
6:30.targetText: So they asked Him, “What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You? What will You do?

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of "see".

6:31.sourceText: οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν τὸ μάννα ἔφαγον ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, καθώς ἐστιν γεγραμμένον Ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν.
6:31.targetText: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:32.sourceText: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τὸν ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἀλλ’ ὁ Πατήρ μου δίδωσιν ὑμῖν τὸν ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τὸν ἀληθινόν·
6:32.targetText: Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The repeated article before ἀληθινόν has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English cleft frame ("it was … who") with no Greek counterpart.
English cleft frame ("it was … who") with no Greek counterpart.
English cleft frame ("it is … who") with no Greek counterpart.
English cleft frame ("it is … who") with no Greek counterpart.

6:33.sourceText: ὁ γὰρ ἄρτος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ καταβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ζωὴν διδοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ.
6:33.targetText: For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”

groups.note: ὁ καταβαίνων ("the one coming down") is masculine like ἄρτος, so it can also be read "that which comes down".
The dative τῷ κόσμῳ supplies "to".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:34.sourceText: εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτόν Κύριε, πάντοτε δὸς ἡμῖν τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον.
6:34.targetText: “Sir,” they said, “give us this bread at all times.”

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed; BSB puts the quotation first.
πρὸς αὐτόν ("to Him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:35.sourceText: εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος τῆς ζωῆς· ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρὸς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ πεινάσῃ, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ διψήσει πώποτε.
6:35.targetText: Jesus answered, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst.

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ ἐρχόμενος ("the one coming") form one unit.
οὐ μή … πώποτε ("not … ever") is rendered "never".

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτοῖς ("to them") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:36.sourceText: ἀλλ’ εἶπον ὑμῖν ὅτι καὶ ἑωράκατέ με καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε.
6:36.targetText: But as I stated, you have seen Me and still you do not believe.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object ὑμῖν ("to you") is not rendered.
ὅτι ("that") is not rendered; BSB makes "as I stated" a side remark.
The first καί of καί … καί ("both … and") is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English turns "I told you that …" into "as I stated".

6:37.sourceText: Πᾶν ὃ δίδωσίν μοι ὁ Πατὴρ πρὸς ἐμὲ ἥξει, καὶ τὸν ἐρχόμενον πρός με οὐ μὴ ἐκβάλω ἔξω,
6:37.targetText: Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never drive away.

groups.note: The neuter Πᾶν ("all that") is rendered "Everyone".
Article and participle τὸν ἐρχόμενον form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The relative pronoun ὅ ("that") is left implicit in English.

6:38.sourceText: ὅτι καταβέβηκα ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ οὐχ ἵνα ποιῶ τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με.
6:38.targetText: For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Me.

groups.note: ἵνα ποιῶ ("to do") is understood again after ἀλλά.
The emphatic τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμόν is rendered "My own will".
Article and participle τοῦ πέμψαντος form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The repeated article before ἐμόν has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:39.sourceText: τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με, ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκέν μοι μὴ ἀπολέσω ἐξ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸ ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
6:39.targetText: And this is the will of Him who sent Me, that I shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day.

groups.note: πᾶν ὅ ("all that") is rendered "those".
μή with ἀπολέσω ("not lose") is rendered "lose none".
ἐξ αὐτοῦ ("of it") resumes πᾶν ὅ; BSB writes "none of those".
The singular αὐτό ("it"), referring back to πᾶν, is rendered "them".

6:40.sourceText: τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Πατρός μου, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ θεωρῶν τὸν Υἱὸν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν ἐγὼ ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
6:40.targetText: For it is My Father’s will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him shall have eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.”

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ θεωρῶν form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:41.sourceText: Ἐγόγγυζον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι εἶπεν Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ καταβὰς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ,
6:41.targetText: At this, the Jews began to grumble about Jesus because He had said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("him") is rendered with the name.
Article and participle ὁ καταβάς form one unit.
